### GPU speedup scales dramatically with platform resolution

Table 8 summarises the spatial benchmark results across three Visium platforms.

: **Table 8.** Spatial transcriptomics benchmark results (RTX 4090, mean of repeats 2-5). {#tbl:spatial_summary}

| Platform | Spots/Bins | CPU total (s) | GPU total (s) | Speedup | CPU RAM (GB) | GPU VRAM (GB) |
|:---------|----------:|---------------:|--------------:|--------:|-------------:|--------------:|
| Visium v1 | 2,695 | 10.0 | 6.0 | 1.7x | 1.3 | 12.9 |
| Visium HD 8 um | 393,543 | 4,068 | 79 | 51.6x | 8.1 | 22.6 |
| Visium HD 2 um | 389,492 | 1,042 | 97 | 10.8x | 10.8 | 22.6 |

End-to-end speedup increased from 1.7x on Visium v1 (2,695 spots) to 51.6x on Visium HD 8 um (393,543 bins) (Fig. 7), demonstrating that GPU acceleration becomes increasingly valuable as spatial resolution increases.

![**Figure 7.** Total pipeline wall time (CPU vs GPU) for three Visium spatial platforms on a single RTX 4090. End-to-end speedups range from 1.7x (Visium v1, 2,695 spots) to 51.6x (Visium HD 8 um, 393,543 bins). Error bars: standard deviation across repeats 2-5 (repeat 1 excluded for JIT warmup). HD 2 um was subsampled to 400k bins due to local VRAM constraints.](../figures/fig7_spatial_speedup.png)

The dominant contributor to the HD 8 um speedup was co-occurrence analysis, which achieved a 3,272x speedup (from 3,573 s on CPU to 1.09 s on GPU; Fig. 8).
The CPU implementation computes pairwise cluster co-occurrence across distance intervals with O(n^2) complexity per interval, while the GPU implementation parallelises this computation across all bins and intervals simultaneously.
At 393,543 bins with 7 Leiden clusters, co-occurrence alone consumed 88% of the CPU pipeline time.

![**Figure 8.** Per-step GPU speedup for Visium HD 8 um (393,543 bins). Co-occurrence analysis achieves a 3,272x speedup (CPU: 3,573 s to GPU: 1.09 s), the single largest acceleration measured in this study. Spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I, Geary's C) shows 162-163x speedup. Steps without GPU implementations (spatial_neighbors, nhood_enrichment) remain at 1.0x.](../figures/fig8_spatial_perstep.png)

Other large GPU advantages on HD 8 um included PCA (257x), normalisation (176x), spatial autocorrelation (162-163x), and UMAP (159x).
Leiden clustering achieved a 16x speedup, and k-NN graph construction achieved 20x.

: **Table 9.** Per-step wall time and GPU speedup for spatial-specific operations on Visium HD 8 um (393,543 bins), the platform showing the largest overall speedup. Steps labelled "CPU-only" in the Speedup column lack a GPU implementation in rapids-singlecell 0.14.1; the "GPU (s)" value for those rows reports the wall time of the CPU fallback executed transparently inside the GPU pipeline, not a GPU-accelerated measurement. {#tbl:spatial_steps}

| Step | CPU (s) | GPU (s) | Speedup |
|:-----|--------:|--------:|--------:|
| Co-occurrence | 3,573 | 1.09 | 3,272x |
| PCA | 72.8 | 0.28 | 257x |
| Normalisation | 0.65 | 0.004 | 176x |
| Moran's I | 47.9 | 0.30 | 162x |
| Geary's C | 47.4 | 0.29 | 163x |
| UMAP | 194.3 | 1.22 | 159x |
| HVG selection | 0.94 | 0.012 | 76x |
| Expression neighbours | 39.4 | 2.00 | 20x |
| Leiden clustering | 19.2 | 1.17 | 16x |
| Spatial neighbours | 55.9 | 57.4 | 1.0x (CPU-only) |
| Nhood enrichment | 11.8 | 11.4 | 1.0x (CPU-only) |

Visium HD 2 um showed a lower overall speedup (10.8x) despite a similar bin count (389,492) because co-occurrence analysis was skipped (>500 clusters exceeded the O(k^2) memory threshold).
Without this step, UMAP dominated the GPU pipeline time (92x speedup, but consuming 92% of the 97 s total GPU time).

On Visium v1, the modest 1.7x overall speedup reflects the small dataset size (2,695 spots): GPU kernel launch overhead is not amortised, and CPU-only steps (spatial neighbours, ligand-receptor) dominate.

Three pipeline steps lacked GPU implementations and constituted the GPU pipeline's primary bottleneck: spatial neighbours (Delaunay triangulation via scipy.spatial, ~55 s on all HD platforms), neighbourhood enrichment (CPU-only), and ligand-receptor interaction (CPU-only, Visium v1 only).
Spatial neighbours alone represented 57-73% of total GPU pipeline time on HD platforms.

### Spatial concordance: near-perfect for spatial statistics, divergent for clustering at high resolution

Spatial autocorrelation concordance was near-perfect across all platforms (Table 10, Fig. 9).

![**Figure 9.** Concordance between CPU and GPU spatial analysis pipelines across three Visium platforms. Spatial autocorrelation statistics (Moran's I, Geary's C) show near-perfect agreement (Spearman rho >= 0.9995). SVG Jaccard overlap of the top 50 genes equals 1.0 for all platforms. Cluster concordance (ARI) degrades at HD 2 um resolution (0.080) due to algorithmic differences between cugraph and leidenalg Leiden implementations at high granularity.](../figures/fig9_spatial_concordance.png)
Moran's I and Geary's C Spearman correlations between CPU and GPU exceeded 0.9995 in all cases.
The top-50 spatially variable genes were identical (Jaccard = 1.0) across all three platforms, confirming that GPU-accelerated spatial autocorrelation produces scientifically equivalent results.
At the FDR < 0.05 threshold, SVG overlap remained high: 100% (Visium v1), 99.9% (HD 8 um), and 98.2% (HD 2 um).

: **Table 10.** Spatial concordance between CPU and GPU pipelines. SVG Jaccard reports the overlap of top-N spatially variable genes ranked by Moran's I. {#tbl:spatial_concordance}

| Metric | Visium v1 | HD 8 um | HD 2 um |
|:-------|----------:|------------:|------------:|
| Moran's I Spearman rho | 1.0000 | 0.9999 | 1.0000 |
| Geary's C Spearman rho | 1.0000 | 0.9995 | 0.9999 |
| SVG Jaccard (top 50) | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| SVG Jaccard (FDR < 0.05) | 1.000 | 0.999 | 0.982 |
| Cluster ARI | 0.856 | 0.974 | 0.080 |
| Cluster NMI | 0.892 | 0.940 | 0.667 |
| N clusters (CPU / GPU) | 16 / 15 | 7 / 3 | 2,559 / 538 |

Expression-based Leiden clustering showed platform-dependent concordance.
On Visium v1 (ARI = 0.856, NMI = 0.892) and HD 8 um (ARI = 0.974, NMI = 0.940), concordance was high, consistent with the scRNA-seq results.
However, on HD 2 um, clustering diverged substantially (ARI = 0.080, NMI = 0.667): the CPU pipeline identified 2,559 clusters while the GPU pipeline found 538.
This 4.75x difference in cluster granularity arises from algorithmic differences between the leidenalg (CPU) and cuGraph (GPU) Leiden implementations, which are amplified at high resolution where the graph has many near-degenerate partitions.
Subsampling from 6.3 million to 389,492 bins also disrupts spatial contiguity, compounding the effect.
This is a known limitation of comparing stochastic graph-partitioning algorithms across implementations, not a deficiency of GPU computation per se.

### Memory usage is modest across spatial platforms

Peak GPU VRAM was 12.9 GB on Visium v1 and plateaued at 22.6 GB for both HD platforms (Table 8), well within the RTX 4090's 24 GB capacity.
CPU RAM ranged from 1.3 GB (Visium v1) to 10.8 GB (HD 2 um).
These modest requirements suggest that spatial benchmarks at full Visium HD resolution (6.3M bins at 2 um) would fit comfortably within DGX H100 memory.

### End-to-end and per-step GPU speedup on three Visium platforms

Table 8 summarises the spatial benchmark on the three platforms.

: **Table 8.** Spatial transcriptomics benchmark: mean +/- SD of five repeats (n = 5, ddof = 1), each in a fresh process. CPU: one DGX H100 node (`poddgx02`, 100 CPUs), the reference; GPU: one RTX 4090. Speedup: ratio of mean totals with 95% bootstrap interval; the next column uses the 128-thread workstation CPU as reference. At Visium HD 8 um the totals include co-occurrence, whose GPU result with rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 was incorrect (see text); without co-occurrence the totals are 616 s (CPU) and 89.7 s (GPU) and the speedup is 6.9x (6.8-6.9) (6.1x with the workstation CPU). Memory: mean of the per-repeat peaks in GiB; GPU VRAM is the device-wide NVML reading and includes the RMM pool. {#tbl:spatial_summary}

| Platform | Spots/bins | CPU total (s) | GPU total (s) | Speedup | Speedup, workstation CPU | CPU RAM (GiB) | GPU VRAM (GiB) |
|:---------|----------:|---------------:|--------------:|--------:|--------:|-------------:|--------------:|
| Visium v1 | 2,695 | 33.9 +/- 1.0 | 24.0 +/- 0.2 | 1.41x (1.38-1.45) | 1.61x | 0.97 | 12.74 |
| Visium HD 8 um | 393,543 | 719 +/- 3 | 92.2 +/- 0.7 | 7.80x (7.75-7.85) | 6.69x | 6.95 | 22.74 |
| Visium HD 2 um (random 400k-bin subsample) | 389,492 | 1,146 +/- 50 | 109.9 +/- 0.8 | 10.43x (10.15-10.82) | 9.39x | 7.95 | 22.73 |

Against the DGX CPU reference, end-to-end GPU speedups were 1.4x on Visium v1 (2,695 spots), 6.9x on Visium HD 8 um (393,543 bins; co-occurrence excluded, see below) and 10.4x on the random 400k-bin subsample of Visium HD 2 um (389,492 bins after QC) (Table 8, Fig. 7).
With the 128-thread workstation CPU as reference they were 1.6x, 6.1x and 9.4x: the choice of CPU changed the speedup by 10-14%, in different directions per platform.
Visium HD 8 um and the 2 um subsample have similar numbers of bins but ran different steps (co-occurrence and neighbourhood enrichment were skipped at 2 um, see below), so the order of the speedups does not show an effect of resolution.

![**Figure 7.** Total pipeline wall time on three Visium platforms: CPU reference (one DGX H100 node, 100 CPUs) and GPU (one RTX 4090), mean of five repeats, each in a fresh process; error bars: SD. Labels give the speedup (ratio of means). At Visium HD 8 um the bars include co-occurrence, whose GPU result with rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 was incorrect (see text); the dashed lines mark the totals without it (6.9x). Visium HD 2 um was randomly subsampled to 400,000 bins (389,492 after QC) to fit in the 24 GiB of the RTX 4090.](../figures/fig7_spatial_speedup.png)

At Visium HD 8 um, with the same 4 cell groups as the CPU, the GPU co-occurrence computed with rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 was incorrect: it matched the CPU result within an absolute tolerance of 0.001 in only 8 of 49 distance intervals, because the number of bin pairs within the larger distance thresholds exceeds the range of its 32-bit integer counters.
The GPU co-occurrence of the original March runs had the same defect.
With rapids-singlecell 0.15.1 the GPU result matched the CPU in 49 of 49 intervals (maximum absolute difference 0.00022) at unchanged runtime (0.15.1/0.14.1 time ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.95-1.00).
In this separate check, co-occurrence with 0.15.1 took 4.41 s against 103 s on the DGX CPU (23.4x, 95% CI 23.3-23.6); because the check ran outside the pipeline and the pipeline result was incorrect, co-occurrence is excluded from the Visium HD speedups.
Squidpy counts co-occurring cluster pairs with a Numba-parallel loop over all pairs of bins for each distance interval (O(n^2) per interval); rapids-singlecell performs the same counting on the GPU.
On the DGX CPU, co-occurrence took 14.4% of the pipeline time at Visium HD 8 um.

![**Figure 8.** Per-step GPU speedup on Visium HD 8 um (393,543 bins) against the DGX CPU reference: ratio of means over five repeats; error bars: 95% bootstrap interval. The largest speedups were for UMAP (197x) and Geary's C (122x); Moran's I reached 20.8x. Spatial neighbours and neighbourhood enrichment ran in Squidpy on the CPU in both pipelines (open circles; 0.80x and 1.1x). Co-occurrence (open diamond) is the speedup of the separate check with rapids-singlecell 0.15.1 (23.4x), because the pipeline result with 0.14.1 was incorrect (see text).](../figures/fig8_spatial_perstep.png)

On Visium HD 8 um the GPU accelerated UMAP 197x, Geary's C 122x, PCA (with scaling) 37.0x, normalisation 30.4x and Moran's I 20.8x; expression neighbours and Leiden clustering were accelerated 13.5x and 12.9x, and data loading, QC and HVG selection ran at 0.99x, 0.89x and 1.8x (Table 9, Fig. 8).
As in the scRNA-seq pipeline, CPU expression neighbour search ran pynndescent on one Numba thread (Methods), so its speedup is relative to a single-threaded search.

: **Table 9.** Per-step wall time and GPU speedup on Visium HD 8 um (393,543 bins): mean +/- SD of five repeats, each in a fresh process; CPU reference: one DGX H100 node (100 CPUs); speedup: ratio of means with 95% bootstrap interval. Spatial neighbours and neighbourhood enrichment have no GPU implementation in rapids-singlecell 0.14.1: the GPU pipeline calls Squidpy on the CPU, so the GPU column for these rows is CPU time on the workstation. PCA includes scaling. CPU expression neighbour search ran on one Numba thread (Methods). Co-occurrence: the GPU result with rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 was incorrect (see text), so no GPU time or speedup is reported (n.r.); with 0.15.1, in a separate check, it took 4.41 s (23.4x). The total includes co-occurrence. {#tbl:spatial_steps}

| Step | CPU (s) | GPU (s) | Speedup |
|:-----|--------:|--------:|--------:|
| Data loading | 3.87 +/- 0.15 | 3.93 +/- 0.08 | 0.99x (0.96-1.02) |
| QC and filtering | 2.72 +/- 0.09 | 3.07 +/- 0.04 | 0.89x (0.86-0.91) |
| Normalisation | 2.62 +/- 0.14 | 0.0861 +/- 0.0030 | 30.4x (29.1-32.1) |
| HVG selection | 1.03 +/- 0.06 | 0.579 +/- 0.059 | 1.8x (1.6-1.9) |
| PCA | 33.7 +/- 0.1 | 0.909 +/- 0.028 | 37.0x (36.1-37.9) |
| Expression neighbours | 58.1 +/- 0.2 | 4.29 +/- 0.11 | 13.5x (13.2-13.7) |
| Leiden clustering | 21.2 +/- 0.2 | 1.65 +/- 0.02 | 12.9x (12.7-13.1) |
| UMAP | 269 +/- 5 | 1.366 +/- 0.007 | 197x (194-200) |
| Spatial neighbours (CPU in both) | 45.2 +/- 0.3 | 56.3 +/- 0.9 | 0.80x (0.79-0.81) |
| Moran's I | 82.6 +/- 1.4 | 3.98 +/- 0.32 | 20.8x (19.4-21.9) |
| Geary's C | 82.1 +/- 2.0 | 0.671 +/- 0.003 | 122x (120-125) |
| Co-occurrence | 103.2 +/- 0.3 | n.r. | n.r. |
| Neighbourhood enrichment (CPU in both) | 13.5 +/- 0.2 | 12.8 +/- 0.4 | 1.1x (1.0-1.1) |
| Total | 719 +/- 3 | 92.2 +/- 0.7 | 7.80x (7.75-7.85) |

On the Visium HD 2 um subsample, CPU Leiden returned 3,027 groups, so co-occurrence and neighbourhood enrichment were skipped (more than 500 groups, Methods) and the totals contain fewer steps than at Visium HD 8 um.
UMAP, the largest CPU cost (72.0% of the CPU time), ran 89.4x faster on the GPU; the GPU pipeline time (110 s) was dominated by spatial neighbours (50.4%) and data loading (27.8%).

On Visium v1 (2,695 spots) the end-to-end speedup was 1.4x: ligand-receptor analysis, run in Squidpy on the CPU in both pipelines, took 38.2% of the GPU pipeline time, and QC (0.18x), Leiden (0.27x), Moran's I (0.51x) and PCA (0.67x) were slower on the GPU than on the CPU.

Three steps ran in Squidpy on the CPU inside the GPU pipeline: spatial neighbours (Delaunay triangulation via scipy.spatial), neighbourhood enrichment and ligand-receptor analysis (Visium v1 only).
On the two Visium HD platforms spatial neighbours took 45.2 s and 45.0 s on the DGX CPU and 56.3 s and 55.4 s in the GPU pipeline on the workstation CPU, 61.1% (HD 8 um) and 50.4% (HD 2 um subsample) of the GPU pipeline time.

### Spatial concordance: close for spatial statistics, divergent for clustering on the Visium HD 2 um subsample

Spatial autocorrelation statistics agreed closely between CPU and GPU on all three platforms (Table 10, Fig. 9).

![**Figure 9.** Concordance between the CPU reference (DGX node) and GPU spatial pipelines on three Visium platforms, CPU repeat k against GPU repeat k (k = 1-5); points: mean of the five pairs, bars: range where the pairs differ. Left: Spearman rho of per-gene Moran's I and Geary's C over 2,000 HVGs, and Jaccard index (J) of spatially variable gene (SVG) sets ranked by Moran's I (top 50, 100 and 200, and FDR < 0.05). Right: adjusted Rand index and normalised mutual information of the expression-based Leiden partitions. On the Visium HD 2 um subsample the partitions diverge (ARI 0.071): CPU Leiden (igraph, 2 iterations) returned 3,027 groups and GPU Leiden (cuGraph, up to 100 iterations) 538; the number of CPU groups also depends on the CPU machine (Table 10).](../figures/fig9_spatial_concordance.png)

Moran's I and Geary's C Spearman correlations between CPU and GPU were at least 0.9995 in all cases.
The top-50 spatially variable genes by Moran's I formed the same set on CPU and GPU on all three platforms (Jaccard = 1.000); for the top 100 and top 200 the Jaccard index was 1.000 on Visium v1 and 0.980 on both Visium HD platforms.
At FDR < 0.05, the Jaccard index of the SVG sets was 1.000 (Visium v1), 0.999 (HD 8 um) and 0.982 (HD 2 um subsample).

: **Table 10.** Spatial concordance between the CPU reference (DGX node) and GPU pipelines, CPU repeat k against GPU repeat k (k = 1-5): a single value when it is the same in the five pairs, otherwise the range. SVG Jaccard reports the overlap of spatially variable genes ranked by Moran's I. Co-occurrence and neighbourhood enrichment were skipped on the HD 2 um subsample (more than 500 groups); at Visium HD 8 um the GPU co-occurrence is the incorrect result of rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 (see text). N clusters: groups returned by each pipeline's own Leiden run in each repeat. With the workstation CPU as reference, CPU Leiden returned 16, 7 and 2,559 groups and the ARI was 0.856, 0.972-0.975 and 0.084. {#tbl:spatial_concordance}

| Metric | Visium v1 | HD 8 um | Visium HD 2 um (random 400k-bin subsample) |
|:-------|----------:|------------:|------------:|
| Moran's I Spearman rho | 1.0000 | 0.9999 | 1.0000 |
| Geary's C Spearman rho | 1.0000 | 0.9995 | 0.9999 |
| SVG Jaccard (top 50) | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| SVG Jaccard (top 100) | 1.000 | 0.980 | 0.980 |
| SVG Jaccard (top 200) | 1.000 | 0.980 | 0.980 |
| SVG Jaccard (FDR < 0.05) | 1.000 | 0.999 | 0.982 |
| Cluster ARI | 0.856 | 0.971-0.974 | 0.071 |
| Cluster NMI | 0.892 | 0.936-0.942 | 0.636 |
| N clusters (CPU / GPU) | 16 / 15 | 4 / 3-4 | 3,027 / 538 |
| Co-occurrence Spearman rho | 1.0000 | 0.1118 (0.14.1) | n.r. |
| Neighbourhood enrichment Spearman rho | 0.9977-0.9982 | 1.0000 | n.r. |

Expression-based Leiden clustering agreed on Visium v1 (ARI 0.856, NMI 0.892) and Visium HD 8 um (ARI 0.971-0.974, NMI 0.936-0.942 over the five repeat pairs), where GPU Leiden returned 3 groups in four repeats and 4 in one, against 4 for the DGX CPU (7 for the workstation CPU).
On the Visium HD 2 um subsample the partitions diverged (ARI 0.071, NMI 0.636): CPU Leiden returned 3,027 clusters on the DGX reference and GPU Leiden 538, in each of the five repeats.
The number of CPU clusters depended on the CPU machine (2,559 on the 128-thread workstation).
This 5.63-fold difference in cluster granularity coincides with the use of two Leiden implementations with different settings (igraph with 2 iterations on the CPU, cuGraph with up to 100 iterations on the GPU); we did not test which of the two factors, or the subsampling, causes it.
The 2 um subsample retains 389,492 of 6.3 million bins; we did not test whether its sparsity contributes to the fragmented partition.

### Memory use on spatial platforms

GPU memory readings (NVML, device-wide) reflect the RMM memory pool: 12.59 GiB was reserved before data loading in every GPU run, and the peak reading was 12.74 GiB on Visium v1, 22.74 GiB on Visium HD 8 um and 22.73 GiB on the HD 2 um subsample (95% of the 24.0 GiB of the RTX 4090); the 2 um data had to be subsampled to fit (Methods).
Peak CPU RAM ranged from 0.97 GiB (Visium v1) to 7.95 GiB (HD 2 um subsample) on the DGX CPU reference, and reached 11.30 GiB in the GPU pipeline (Visium HD 8 um).
Whether the full-resolution Visium HD 2 um dataset (6.3 million bins) fits in GPU memory was not tested; the CPU pipeline densifies the HVG matrix, which at this size would need about 50 GB (47 GiB) in float32.

edits.old: The extension to spatial transcriptomics shows that GPU advantages are even more pronounced for spatial-specific operations, with co-occurrence analysis achieving over three orders of magnitude speedup.
edits.new: The spatial benchmark, repeated with a fresh process per repeat and the same cell groups on CPU and GPU, gave end-to-end speedups of 1.4x (Visium v1), 6.9x (Visium HD 8 um, co-occurrence excluded) and 10.4x (Visium HD 2 um subsample) against the 100-CPU DGX reference (1.6x, 6.1x and 9.4x against the workstation CPU); among the spatial-specific steps of the pipeline only spatial autocorrelation gained substantially, and GPU co-occurrence at Visium HD 8 um was incorrect in rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 (correct, and 23.4x faster than the DGX CPU, with 0.15.1).

edits.anchor: Beyond scRNA-seq, the extension to spatial transcriptomics demonstrates
edits.old: Beyond scRNA-seq, the extension to spatial transcriptomics demonstrates that GPU acceleration becomes increasingly impactful for computationally intensive spatial statistics. The 3,272x speedup achieved for co-occurrence analysis on Visium HD 8 um data is, to our knowledge, the largest GPU speedup reported for any spatial transcriptomics operation, reflecting the O(n^2) algorithmic complexity of the CPU implementation which the GPU effectively parallelises across thousands of bins and spatial distance intervals simultaneously. Spatial autocorrelation statistics (Moran's I, Geary's C) achieved similarly impressive speedups of 162-170x with near-perfect numerical concordance (rho >= 0.9995), meaning that scientists can obtain identical rankings of spatially variable genes in seconds rather than minutes. The remaining CPU-only operations (spatial neighbours computation via Delaunay triangulation, neighbourhood enrichment, and ligand-receptor analysis) represent clear opportunities for future GPU-native implementations and likely harbour substantial additional speedup potential.
edits.new: In the spatial benchmark, the GPU advantage was concentrated in a few steps rather than spread across spatial statistics as a whole. At Visium HD 8 um, GPU co-occurrence in rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 was incorrect: on the same 4 cell groups as the CPU it matched the CPU result at only 8 of 49 distances, because its 32-bit pair counters overflow at this number of bins. With rapids-singlecell 0.15.1 it matched at 49 of 49 distances in the same time (time ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.95-1.00), so we excluded co-occurrence from the Visium HD speedups; in a separate check the corrected version was 23.4x faster than the DGX CPU. Spatial autocorrelation statistics were accelerated 20.8-21.0x (Moran's I) and 122.4-128.9x (Geary's C) on Visium HD (9.3-13.1x and 55.1-75.6x against the workstation CPU), with near-perfect numerical concordance (Spearman rho >= 0.9995); the top-50 spatially variable genes formed the same set on CPU and GPU, and each statistic took 0.7-4.0 s on the GPU instead of 82-86 s on the CPU reference. On the GPU, Moran's I remained slower than Geary's C (about 4 s against less than 1 s), and on Visium v1 it was not accelerated (0.51x). In rapids-singlecell 0.14.1, spatial neighbour computation and neighbourhood enrichment have no GPU implementation and ran on the CPU inside the GPU pipeline (0.80x and 1.1x at Visium HD 8 um); ligand-receptor analysis, run on Visium v1 only, has a GPU implementation in rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 that our pipeline did not use (Squidpy on the CPU in both pipelines, 0.96x).

edits.anchor: A notable finding from spatial analysis concerns clustering at extreme resolution.
edits.old: A notable finding from spatial analysis concerns clustering at extreme resolution. The dramatic divergence at Visium HD 2 um (ARI = 0.080) is not specific to GPU versus CPU comparison; rather, it reflects the fundamental sensitivity of stochastic graph-partitioning algorithms to implementation details when the solution landscape contains many near-degenerate partitions. At 389,492 spatial bins with resolution parameter 0.1, local optima abound, and the leidenalg (CPU) and cuGraph (GPU) implementations explore this landscape through different vertex orderings and local heuristics. This observation suggests that users working at ultra-high spatial resolution should not rely on a single run of any Leiden implementation, but instead employ consensus clustering approaches or spatial-aware alternative methods that explicitly account for tissue geometry.
edits.new: A notable finding from spatial analysis concerns clustering on the Visium HD 2 um subsample. At 389,492 spatial bins and resolution 0.1, the igraph (CPU) and cuGraph (GPU) implementations returned very different partitions (ARI 0.071): CPU Leiden returned 3,027 clusters on the DGX reference and 2,559 on the workstation and 538 on the GPU, each the same in all five repeats. The divergence is therefore systematic between implementations and machines rather than run-to-run stochasticity; we did not test whether different seeds of the same implementation diverge to a similar extent. Users working at this resolution should therefore check how stable Leiden partitions are across implementations and settings before interpreting them.

edits.anchor: For spatial transcriptomics, GPU acceleration delivers 51.6x end-to-end speedup on Visium HD, with co-occurrence analysis achieving a 3,272x speedup and spatial autocorrelation concordance exceeding 0.9995.
edits.old: For spatial transcriptomics, GPU acceleration delivers 51.6x end-to-end speedup on Visium HD, with co-occurrence analysis achieving a 3,272x speedup and spatial autocorrelation concordance exceeding 0.9995.
edits.new: For spatial transcriptomics on one RTX 4090, end-to-end speedups against a 100-CPU DGX node were 1.4x on Visium v1, 6.9x on Visium HD 8 um with co-occurrence excluded and 10.4x on a random 400k-bin subsample of Visium HD 2 um; Moran's I and Geary's C agreed between CPU and GPU (Spearman rho at least 0.9995). The GPU co-occurrence of rapids-singlecell 0.14.1 was incorrect at Visium HD 8 um because of 32-bit integer overflow; version 0.15.1 corrects it at unchanged runtime.
